examples.title: Common attribute types on a control
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
cmds.addAttr(ctrl, longName="stretch", attributeType="double", minValue=0, maxValue=1, defaultValue=0, keyable=True)
cmds.addAttr(ctrl, longName="twist", attributeType="doubleAngle", keyable=True)
cmds.addAttr(ctrl, longName="space", attributeType="enum", enumName="World:Local:Hand", keyable=True)
cmds.addAttr(ctrl, longName="showJoints", attributeType="bool", defaultValue=True)
cmds.setAttr(ctrl + ".showJoints", channelBox=True)
cmds.addAttr(ctrl, longName="notes", dataType="string")

print(cmds.listAttr(ctrl, userDefined=True))  # ['stretch', 'twist', 'space', 'showJoints', 'notes']
print(cmds.attributeQuery("stretch", node=ctrl, range=True))  # [0.0, 1.0]

examples.title: A compound attribute (like translate)
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

node = cmds.createNode("transform", name="aim")
cmds.addAttr(node, longName="aimVector", attributeType="double3")
for axis in "XYZ":
    cmds.addAttr(node, longName="aimVector" + axis, attributeType="double", parent="aimVector")

cmds.setAttr(node + ".aimVector", 1, 0, 0)
print(cmds.getAttr(node + ".aimVector"))  # [(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)]

examples.title: A multi (array) of messages
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

rig = cmds.createNode("network", name="rigData")
cmds.addAttr(rig, longName="controls", attributeType="message", multi=True)

for i, name in enumerate(("hand_ctrl", "elbow_ctrl")):
    ctrl = cmds.circle(name=name)[0]
    cmds.connectAttr(ctrl + ".message", "%s.controls[%d]" % (rig, i))

print(cmds.listConnections(rig + ".controls"))  # ['hand_ctrl', 'elbow_ctrl']

examples.title: Add only if missing, and edit an existing attribute
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
for _ in range(2):
    if not cmds.attributeQuery("blend", node=ctrl, exists=True):
        cmds.addAttr(ctrl, longName="blend", attributeType="double", keyable=True)

cmds.addAttr(ctrl + ".blend", edit=True, minValue=0, maxValue=10)
cmds.addAttr(ctrl + ".blend", edit=True, niceName="IK Blend")
print(cmds.attributeQuery("blend", node=ctrl, maximum=True))  # [10.0]
print(cmds.attributeQuery("blend", node=ctrl, niceName=True))  # 'IK Blend'

gotchas: Numeric and compound types use `attributeType`; strings, matrices and arrays use `dataType`. Mixing them up fails.
Compound children must be added right after the parent, with `parent=`, and you must add all of them before using the attribute.
`addAttr` fails if the attribute exists. Check with `attributeQuery(name, node=node, exists=True)` first.
New attributes aren't keyable unless you pass `keyable=True`, so they don't show in the Channel Box.
Edit with `addAttr(node + ".attr", edit=True, ...)`: the plug goes in the object argument.

summary: Constrains an object's orientation so one of its axes points at the targets.
returns: The constraint node name, in a list.

flags.worldUpType: How world up is found: `"scene"`, `"object"` (point at the object), `"objectrotation"` (use the object's axis), `"vector"` or `"none"`.

examples.title: Point an object's X axis at a target
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.setAttr(target + ".translate", 0, 0, -10)
eye = cmds.polyCube(name="eye")[0]

cmds.aimConstraint(target, eye, aimVector=(1, 0, 0), upVector=(0, 1, 0), worldUpType="scene")
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.getAttr(eye + ".rotate")[0]])  # [0.0, 90.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Use an up object to control twist
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.setAttr(target + ".translateX", 10)
up = cmds.spaceLocator(name="up")[0]
cmds.setAttr(up + ".translateZ", 5)
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

con = cmds.aimConstraint(target, obj, aimVector=(1, 0, 0), upVector=(0, 1, 0), worldUpType="object", worldUpObject=up)[0]
print(cmds.aimConstraint(con, query=True, worldUpObject=True))  # ['up']
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.getAttr(obj + ".rotate")[0]])  # [90.0, 0.0, 0.0]

gotchas: `aimVector` and `upVector` are in the object's local space. They must not be parallel.
With `worldUpType="scene"`, twist is unstable when the aim direction gets close to the world up. Use an up object or vector.

flags.target: Particle object to map onto. Can be repeated.
flags.type: Type of texture node to create.
flags.destAttr: Per-particle attribute that receives the values.

art3dPaintCtx.name: art3dPaintCtx
summary: Creates or edits the 3D Paint tool, which paints textures directly on objects.

flags.keepaspectratio: Keep the aspect ratio when resizing textures.
flags.brushtype: Brush type, e.g. `"ArtisanBrush"` or a Paint Effects brush.
flags.alphablendmode: How paint blends: `"Default"`, `"Lighten"`, `"Darken"`, `"Difference"`, `"Exclusion"`, `"Hard Light"`, `"Soft Light"`, `"Multiply"`, `"Screen"`, `"Overlay"`, `"Dodge"` or `"Burn"`.
flags.painttxtattrname: Name of the texture attribute being painted.
flags.soloAsDiffuse: Show the painted attribute as the diffuse color.
flags.commonattr: Attributes common to all selected shaders.
flags.extendFillColor: Extend the fill color past UV borders to avoid seams.
flags.filetxtaspectratio: Aspect ratio of new texture files.
flags.alwaysKeepFile: Keep texture files even if they're not saved with the scene.
flags.attrnames: Attribute to paint, such as `"color"` or `"transparency"`.
flags.shadernames: Query only: shaders on the selected objects.
flags.reloadtexfile: Reload the texture files from disk.
flags.assigntxt: Assign file textures to the selected objects.
flags.fileformat: Image format for new textures, e.g. `"iff"` or `"tif"`.
flags.exists: Returns True if a tool context with the given name exists.
flags.history: Turn construction history on for objects the tool creates.
flags.name: Name for the new tool context. Pass it to `setToolTo` to make the tool active.
flags.image3: Third icon image for the tool.
flags.image1: First icon image for the tool, as shown in the toolbox and tool settings.
flags.image2: Second icon image for the tool.
flags.expandfilename: When exporting maps, add the object's name to the file name.
flags.outwhilepaint: Keep showing the brush outline while painting.
flags.makeStroke: Stroke data used to replay a recorded stroke. Mainly internal.
flags.lowerradius: Lower brush radius, used when pressure affects the radius.
flags.exportfiletype: Image format of exported maps, e.g. `"iff"` or `"tif"`.
flags.selectclonesource: Pick the source point for the clone brush.
flags.stampSpacing: Distance between stamps along a stroke, as a fraction of the brush radius.
flags.brushalignment: Rotate the brush to follow the stroke direction.
flags.projective: Project strokes from the view instead of painting along the surface.
flags.lastRecorderCmd: The last recorded stroke command. Mainly internal.
flags.record: Record strokes so they can be replayed.
flags.tablet: Query only: whether a tablet is available.
flags.importfileload: Load painted values from this image file.
flags.exportfilesizey: Height in pixels of exported maps.
flags.paintoperationtype: Paint operation, e.g. `"Paint"`, `"Smear"`, `"Blur"`, `"Erase"` or `"Clone"`, depending on the tool.
flags.reflectionaboutorigin: Reflect about the world origin instead of the object's center.
flags.exportfilesizex: Width in pixels of exported maps.
flags.preserveclonesource: Keep the clone source point between strokes.
flags.profileShapeFile: Image file used as the brush shape.
flags.surfaceConformedBrushVertices: Make the brush outline follow the surface.
flags.dragSlider: Start an interactive drag to change a brush setting: `"radius"`, `"lowradius"`, `"opacity"`, `"value"`, `"depth"`, `"displacement"`, `"uvvector"` or `"none"`.
flags.importfilemode: Which channel of an imported image to use: `"alpha"`, `"luminance"`, `"red"`, `"green"` or `"blue"`.
flags.showactive: Only show the surfaces being painted.
flags.brushfeedback: Draw extra brush feedback in the viewport.
flags.playbackCursor: Cursor positions for stroke playback. Mainly internal.
flags.paintmode: How strokes are projected onto the surface: `"screen"` or `"tangent"`.
flags.exportfilesave: Export the painted values to this image file.
flags.lastStampName: Name of the last stamp used. Mainly internal.
flags.accopacity: Let opacity build up within a single stroke.
flags.tangentOutline: Draw the brush outline flat on the surface.
flags.dynclonemode: Update the clone source dynamically while painting with a clone brush.
flags.strokesmooth: Smoothing applied to the stroke path.
flags.playbackPressure: Pressure values for stroke playback. Mainly internal.

from maya import cmds

examples.title: Bake a constraint into keys, then remove the constraint
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(target, attribute="translateX", time=1, value=0)
cmds.setKeyframe(target, attribute="translateX", time=10, value=10)

follower = cmds.polyCube(name="follower")[0]
con = cmds.pointConstraint(target, follower)[0]

cmds.bakeResults(follower, time=(1, 10), attribute=["translateX", "translateY", "translateZ"], simulation=True)
cmds.delete(con)

print(cmds.keyframe(follower, attribute="translateX", query=True, keyframeCount=True))  # 10
print(cmds.getAttr(follower + ".translateX", time=10))  # 10.0

examples.title: Bake every other frame
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.expression(string="box.translateY = frame;")

cmds.bakeResults(box, time=(1, 9), sampleBy=2, attribute="translateY")
print(cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, timeChange=True))  # [1.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.0, 9.0]

gotchas: Bake the attributes you need with `attribute=`; otherwise every keyable attribute is baked.
Use `simulation=True` for anything time-dependent (dynamics, expressions reading previous frames), so frames evaluate in order.
The constraint or expression is left in place. Delete it after baking, or pass `disableImplicitControl=True`.
Baked keys replace existing keys in the range unless `preserveOutsideKeys` is used for keys outside it.

examples.title: Create a blend shape with a target
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

base = cmds.polySphere(name="head")[0]
smile = cmds.duplicate(base, name="smile")[0]
cmds.move(0, 0.5, 0, smile + ".vtx[0:20]", relative=True)

bs = cmds.blendShape(smile, base, name="face_bs")[0]
print(cmds.blendShape(bs, query=True, target=True))  # ['smile']
print(cmds.listAttr(bs + ".weight", multi=True))  # ['smile']  (listAttr shows the alias)
print(cmds.aliasAttr(bs, query=True))  # ['smile', 'weight[0]']

examples.title: Drive a target weight by its name
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

base = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
tall = cmds.duplicate(base, name="tall")[0]
cmds.move(0, 1, 0, tall + ".vtx[2:5]", relative=True)
bs = cmds.blendShape(tall, base, name="box_bs")[0]

cmds.setAttr(bs + ".tall", 0.5)
top = cmds.xform(base + ".vtx[2]", query=True, translation=True)
print(round(top[1], 3))  # 1.0

t2 = cmds.duplicate(base, name="deep")[0]

cmds.blendShape(bs, edit=True, target=(base, 1, t2, 1.0))
print(cmds.blendShape(bs, query=True, target=True))  # ['wide', 'deep']
print(cmds.blendShape(bs, query=True, weightCount=True))  # 2

examples.title: In-between target
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

base = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
half = cmds.duplicate(base, name="half")[0]
full = cmds.duplicate(base, name="full")[0]
cmds.move(0, 0.2, 0, half + ".vtx[2:5]", relative=True)
cmds.move(0, 1, 0, full + ".vtx[2:5]", relative=True)

bs = cmds.blendShape(full, base, name="bs")[0]
cmds.blendShape(bs, edit=True, inBetween=True, target=(base, 0, half, 0.5))
cmds.setAttr(bs + ".full", 0.5)
print(round(cmds.xform(base + ".vtx[2]", query=True, translation=True)[1], 3))  # 0.7

gotchas: Target weights are `weight[i]` with an alias named after the target mesh. Use the alias (`bs.smile`) or look it up with `aliasAttr`.
The `target` flag takes a 4-tuple in Python: `(base, targetIndex, targetMesh, fullWeight)`.
Target meshes stay connected; deleting them bakes the shape into the node. Delete them only once you don't need to edit them.
The target must have the same vertex count and order as the base.

from maya import cmds

examples.title: Deform some vertices with a handle
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cl, handle = cmds.cluster(box + ".vtx[2:5]", name="lid")
cmds.move(0, 2, 0, handle, relative=True)

print(cl, handle)  # ('lid', 'lidHandle')
print(round(cmds.xform(box + ".vtx[2]", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)[1], 3))  # 2.5

examples.title: Relative cluster that ignores parent transforms
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
cl, handle = cmds.cluster(box + ".vtx[0]", relative=True)
cmds.parent(handle, grp)
cmds.move(0, 5, 0, grp)

print(round(cmds.xform(box + ".vtx[0]", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)[1], 3))  # -0.5

examples.title: Set per-vertex weights
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cl, handle = cmds.cluster(box + ".vtx[2:5]")
cmds.percent(cl, box + ".vtx[2]", value=0.5)
cmds.move(0, 2, 0, handle, relative=True)

print(round(cmds.xform(box + ".vtx[2]", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)[1], 3))  # 1.5
print(round(cmds.percent(cl, box + ".vtx[2]", query=True, value=True)[0], 3))  # 0.5

gotchas: Names clash with the default cameras: `cluster(name="top")` becomes `top1`. Avoid `persp`, `top`, `front` and `side`.
The handle is created at the center of the components; its pivot, not its translate, is at that position.
Without `relative=True`, moving the handle's parent also moves the points.
Set weights with `percent` or the `weightList` attribute; the cluster has no per-vertex flags.

examples.title: Ask before a destructive action
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

result = cmds.confirmDialog(title="Delete history", message="Delete history on the selected meshes?",
                            button=["Delete", "Cancel"], defaultButton="Delete",
                            cancelButton="Cancel", dismissString="Cancel", icon="warning")
if result == "Delete":
    cmds.delete(cmds.ls(selection=True), constructionHistory=True)

gotchas: Set `cancelButton` and `dismissString` so Esc and closing the window give a predictable answer.

examples.title: Drive one attribute with another
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

driver = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
driven = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(driver + ".rotateY", driven + ".rotateY")

cmds.setAttr(driver + ".rotateY", 30)
print(round(cmds.getAttr(driven + ".rotateY"), 6))  # 30.0  (angles pass through radians, so round)
print(cmds.isConnected(driver + ".rotateY", driven + ".rotateY"))  # True

examples.title: Build a small math network
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.spaceLocator(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.spaceLocator(name="b")[0]
cmds.setAttr(a + ".translateX", 2)
cmds.setAttr(b + ".translateX", 5)

avg = cmds.createNode("plusMinusAverage", name="avg")
cmds.setAttr(avg + ".operation", 3)  # average
cmds.connectAttr(a + ".translate", avg + ".input3D[0]")
cmds.connectAttr(b + ".translate", avg + ".input3D[1]")

mid = cmds.spaceLocator(name="mid")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(avg + ".output3D", mid + ".translate")
print(cmds.getAttr(mid + ".translateX"))  # 3.5

examples.title: Replace an existing connection with `force`
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.spaceLocator(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.spaceLocator(name="b")[0]
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(a + ".translateX", box + ".translateX")

try:
    cmds.connectAttr(b + ".translateX", box + ".translateX")
except RuntimeError:
    print("already connected")  # 'already connected'

cmds.connectAttr(b + ".translateX", box + ".translateX", force=True)
print(cmds.listConnections(box + ".translateX", source=True, destination=False))  # ['b']

examples.title: Connect to the next free element of a multi
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

layer = cmds.createNode("objectSet", name="mySet")
for name in ("a", "b", "c"):
    node = cmds.createNode("transform", name=name)
    cmds.connectAttr(node + ".message", layer + ".dnSetMembers", nextAvailable=True)

print(cmds.getAttr(layer + ".dnSetMembers", multiIndices=True))  # [0, 1, 2]

gotchas: The destination can have only one incoming connection. Use `force=True` to replace it, or `disconnectAttr` first.
`nextAvailable` only works on multi attributes whose index doesn't matter. On others it errors, so find a free index yourself with `getAttr(plug, multiIndices=True)`.
Connecting compound to compound (e.g. `translate` → `translate`) is one connection. You can't also connect a child like `translateX` on the same destination.
Angle values go through radians internally, so a connected rotation of 30 can read back as 29.999999999999996. Round before comparing.
Connecting different units (e.g. an angle into a distance) silently inserts a `unitConversion` node. `listConnections(..., skipConversionNodes=True)` sees past it.

examples.title: Utility nodes for a rig network
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

md = cmds.createNode("multiplyDivide", name="double_md")
cmds.setAttr(md + ".input2X", 2)

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(ctrl + ".translateY", md + ".input1X")
cmds.connectAttr(md + ".outputX", box + ".translateY")

cmds.setAttr(ctrl + ".translateY", 3)
print(cmds.getAttr(box + ".translateY"))  # 6.0

examples.title: Shapes get a transform automatically
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

shape = cmds.createNode("locator", name="myLocShape")
print(shape)  # 'myLocShape'
print(cmds.listRelatives(shape, parent=True))  # ['myLoc']  (named after the shape, minus "Shape")

other = cmds.createNode("locator")
print(cmds.listRelatives(other, parent=True))  # ['locator1']

examples.title: Create under a parent without changing the selection
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
cmds.select(grp)
offset = cmds.createNode("transform", name="offset", parent=grp, skipSelect=True)

print(cmds.ls(offset, long=True))  # ['|grp|offset']
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['grp']

examples.title: Create only if it doesn't exist yet
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

first = cmds.createNode("network", name="settings", shared=True)
second = cmds.createNode("network", name="settings", shared=True)
print(first)  # 'settings'
print(second)  # None  (nothing created, and the existing name isn't returned)
print(cmds.ls(type="network"))  # ['settings']

node = cmds.createNode("network", name="settings", shared=True) or "settings"
print(node)  # 'settings'

gotchas: Shape types (`mesh`, `locator`, `nurbsCurve`…) create a transform too, and return the shape name.
An empty `mesh` has no geometry; you need to connect or build geometry into it. Use `polyCube` and friends for ready-made meshes.
With `shared=True`, a second call returns `None` instead of the existing node. Fall back to the name yourself.
New nodes are selected unless you pass `skipSelect=True`, which matters in scripts that rely on the selection.
Use `shadingNode` for shaders and textures, so they show up correctly in the Hypershade.

examples.title: Set and query the time
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.currentTime(24)
print(cmds.currentTime(query=True))  # 24.0

examples.title: Step through frames to read an evaluated value
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=1, value=0, outTangentType="linear")
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=5, value=8, inTangentType="linear")

values = []
for frame in range(1, 6):
    cmds.currentTime(frame)
    values.append(round(cmds.getAttr(box + ".translateY"), 6))
print(values)  # [0.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0]

examples.title: Change the time without evaluating the scene
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.currentTime(100, update=False)
print(cmds.currentTime(query=True))  # 100.0

gotchas: Changing the time evaluates the scene and redraws viewports, which is slow in loops. For simple values use `getAttr(plug, time=t)` instead.
`update=False` changes the time without evaluating; attribute values won't match the new time until something triggers evaluation.
Time is in the current time unit (see `currentUnit -time`), not always 24 fps frames.

cutKey.name: cutKey
summary: Cuts keys from animation curves into the clipboard, or deletes them.
returns: The number of curves affected.

flags.option: What happens to the gap: `"keys"` (remove keys), `"curve"` (remove the curve segment, shifting later keys), or `"areaCurve"`.
flags.clear: Delete the keys without putting them in the clipboard.
flags.attribute: Only use curves on this attribute. Can be repeated.
flags.shape: Also include curves on the objects' shape nodes.
flags.controlPoints: Also include curves on the objects' control points (vertices, CVs).
flags.animation: Which curves to work on: `"objects"` (all curves on the given objects), `"keys"` (selected keys) or `"keysOrObjects"` (selected keys if any, else the objects). In query mode it takes a boolean.
flags.includeUpperBound: Include keys at the end of a `time` or `float` range. On by default.
flags.time: Time range to use: a single time or `(start, end)`. In MEL, `"start:end"`.
flags.float: Range of float inputs for curves not driven by time, such as driven keys: a single value or `(start, end)`.
flags.index: Range of key indices (0-based): a single index or `(start, end)`.

examples.title: Delete keys in a range
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
for t in (1, 5, 10, 15):
    cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateX", time=t, value=t)

cmds.cutKey(box, attribute="translateX", time=(5, 10), clear=True)
print(cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateX", query=True, timeChange=True))  # [1.0, 15.0]

examples.title: Remove all animation from an attribute
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute=["translateX", "translateY"], time=[1, 10])

cmds.cutKey(box, attribute="translateX", clear=True)
print(cmds.listConnections(box, type="animCurve"))  # ['box_translateY']

examples.title: Cut and paste animation onto another object
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polyCube(name="b")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(a, attribute="rotateY", time=1, value=0)
cmds.setKeyframe(a, attribute="rotateY", time=10, value=90)

cmds.cutKey(a, attribute="rotateY")
cmds.pasteKey(b, attribute="rotateY")
print(cmds.keyframe(a, query=True, keyframeCount=True))  # 0
print(cmds.keyframe(b, attribute="rotateY", query=True, valueChange=True))  # [0.0, 90.0]

gotchas: Without `clear=True`, keys also go to the clipboard, replacing whatever was copied before.
Cutting all keys removes the animation curve, and the attribute keeps its last evaluated value.
`time=(a, b)` includes both ends.

examples.title: Delete construction history but keep the object
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.polyBevel3(cube + ".e[0]")
print(len(cmds.listHistory(cube)) > 2)  # True

cmds.delete(cube, constructionHistory=True)
print(cmds.listHistory(cube))  # ['boxShape']

examples.title: Remove animation, constraints or static curves
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateX", time=[1, 10], value=0)
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=1, value=0)
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=10, value=5)

cmds.delete(box, staticChannels=True)
print(cmds.listConnections(box, type="animCurve"))  # ['box_translateY']

cmds.delete(box, channels=True)
print(cmds.listConnections(box, type="animCurve"))  # None

examples.title: Delete only if it exists
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.group(empty=True, name="old_rig")

for name in ("old_rig", "missing_rig"):
    if cmds.objExists(name):
        cmds.delete(name)
print(cmds.objExists("old_rig"))  # False

cmds.delete(cmds.ls("temp_*"))  # nothing matches: ls returns [] and delete of an empty list is fine

gotchas: `constructionHistory=True` keeps deformers such as skinClusters only if you use Edit > Delete by Type > Non-Deformer History. In scripts, `bakePartialHistory(node, prePostDeformers=True)` is the safer choice on skinned meshes.
Deleting a missing object raises `ValueError`. Check with `objExists` or filter with `ls`.
Deleting a transform deletes its children too.
`channels=True` deletes the animation, not the object.

duplicate.name: duplicate
summary: Duplicates objects. Returns the names of the new objects.
returns: The names of the new objects: the top-level duplicate first, then children unless `returnRootsOnly=True`.

flags.name: Name for the duplicate.
flags.parentOnly: Duplicate only the given object, not its children.
flags.inputConnections: Keep incoming connections on the duplicates.
flags.instanceLeaf: Instance the leaf (shape) nodes instead of copying them.

examples.title: Simple duplicate with a new name
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
copy = cmds.duplicate(box, name="box_copy")[0]
print(copy)  # 'box_copy'
print(cmds.listRelatives(copy, shapes=True))  # ['box_copyShape']

examples.title: Keep the input network, or just the geometry
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(ctrl + ".translateY", box + ".translateY")

plain = cmds.duplicate(box, name="plain")[0]
linked = cmds.duplicate(box, name="linked", inputConnections=True)[0]
print(cmds.listConnections(plain + ".translateY"))  # None
print(cmds.listConnections(linked + ".translateY"))  # ['ctrl']

examples.title: Duplicate a hierarchy and get only the top node
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

rig = cmds.group(empty=True, name="rig")
cmds.parent(cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0], rig)

result = cmds.duplicate(rig, name="rig_copy")
print(result)  # ['rig_copy', 'box']
print(cmds.duplicate(rig, returnRootsOnly=True))  # ['rig1']

examples.title: A clean copy of a deformed mesh (no history)
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.cluster(box)

copy = cmds.duplicate(box, name="baked")[0]
print(cmds.listRelatives(copy, shapes=True))  # ['bakedShape', 'bakedShapeOrig']

for shape in cmds.listRelatives(copy, shapes=True, fullPath=True):
    if cmds.getAttr(shape + ".intermediateObject"):
        cmds.delete(shape)
print(cmds.listRelatives(copy, shapes=True))  # ['bakedShape']

gotchas: Duplicating a deformed mesh copies the intermediate `…ShapeOrig` shape too. Delete intermediate shapes for a clean copy.
Child names in the result are short names and may be ambiguous; use `fullPath=True` if you'll pass them on.
Upstream history isn't copied unless you use `upstreamNodes=True`; incoming connections aren't kept unless you use `inputConnections=True`.

examples.title: Save and open a scene
examples.code:
from maya import cmds
import os, tempfile

path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "shot.ma")
cmds.polyCube(name="box")
cmds.file(rename=path)
cmds.file(save=True, type="mayaAscii")

cmds.file(new=True, force=True)
cmds.file(path, open=True, force=True)
print(cmds.objExists("box"))  # True
print(os.path.basename(cmds.file(query=True, sceneName=True)))  # 'shot.ma'

examples.title: Export the selection and import it with a namespace
examples.code:
from maya import cmds
import os, tempfile

path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "prop.ma")
box = cmds.polyCube(name="crate")[0]
cmds.select(box)
cmds.file(path, exportSelected=True, type="mayaAscii", force=True)

cmds.file(new=True, force=True)
nodes = cmds.file(path, i=True, namespace="prop", returnNewNodes=True)
print(cmds.ls(nodes, type="transform"))  # ['prop:crate']

examples.title: Reference a file and query it
examples.code:
from maya import cmds
import os, tempfile

path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "asset.ma")
cmds.polySphere(name="ball")
cmds.file(rename=path)
cmds.file(save=True, type="mayaAscii")

cmds.file(new=True, force=True)
cmds.file(path, reference=True, namespace="asset")
ref_node = cmds.referenceQuery(path, referenceNode=True)
print(ref_node)  # 'assetRN'
print(cmds.referenceQuery(ref_node, namespace=True))  # ':asset'
print(cmds.referenceQuery("asset:ball", isNodeReferenced=True))  # True

examples.title: Unsaved changes?
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.file(new=True, force=True)
print(cmds.file(query=True, modified=True))  # False
cmds.polyCube()
print(cmds.file(query=True, modified=True))  # True

gotchas: Import is `i=True` in Python (`import` is a reserved word).

examples.title: A list that fills the window with buttons at the bottom
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

if cmds.window("listTool", exists=True):
    cmds.deleteUI("listTool")
win = cmds.window("listTool", title="Scene objects", widthHeight=(300, 400))
form = cmds.formLayout(numberOfDivisions=100)

items = cmds.textScrollList(allowMultiSelection=True, append=cmds.ls(type="transform"))
refresh = cmds.button(label="Refresh")
select = cmds.button(label="Select")

cmds.formLayout(form, edit=True,
    attachForm=[(items, "top", 5), (items, "left", 5), (items, "right", 5),
                (refresh, "left", 5), (refresh, "bottom", 5),
                (select, "right", 5), (select, "bottom", 5)],
    attachControl=[(items, "bottom", 5, refresh)],
    attachPosition=[(refresh, "right", 2, 50), (select, "left", 2, 50)],
    attachNone=[(refresh, "top"), (select, "top")])

cmds.button(refresh, edit=True, command=lambda *_: (
    cmds.textScrollList(items, edit=True, removeAll=True),
    cmds.textScrollList(items, edit=True, append=cmds.ls(type="transform"))))
cmds.button(select, edit=True, command=lambda *_: cmds.select(
    cmds.textScrollList(items, query=True, selectItem=True) or []))
cmds.showWindow(win)

gotchas: Every child needs enough edges attached to know its size and position; unattached controls pile up in the top-left corner.
Use `attachNone` for edges that should follow the control's natural size (like a button's top edge).
`attachPosition` uses `numberOfDivisions` (default 100), so 50 means the middle.

examples.title: Single values and compound values
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.move(1, 2, 3, cube)

print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".translateX"))  # 1.0
print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".translate"))  # [(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)]

tx, ty, tz = cmds.getAttr(cube + ".translate")[0]
print(ty)  # 2.0

examples.title: Value at another time, without changing the current time
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(cube, attribute="translateY", time=1, value=0)
cmds.setKeyframe(cube, attribute="translateY", time=10, value=10)

print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".translateY", time=10))  # 10.0

examples.title: Enum as a name, and attribute state
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setAttr(cube + ".rotateOrder", 2)

print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".rotateOrder"))  # 2
print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".rotateOrder", asString=True))  # 'zxy'

print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".translateX", keyable=True))  # True

examples.title: World matrix of an object
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
cmds.move(0, 5, 0, grp)
child = cmds.spaceLocator(name="loc")[0]
child = cmds.parent(child, grp)[0]
cmds.setAttr(child + ".translate", 0, 0, 0)   # parent keeps world position, so reset local

world = cmds.getAttr(child + ".worldMatrix[0]")
print(world[12:15])  # [0.0, 5.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Existing elements of a multi attribute
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

pma = cmds.createNode("plusMinusAverage")
cmds.setAttr(pma + ".input1D[0]", 1)
cmds.setAttr(pma + ".input1D[4]", 2)

print(cmds.getAttr(pma + ".input1D", multiIndices=True))  # [0, 4]
print(cmds.getAttr(pma + ".input1D", size=True))  # 2

gotchas: Compound attributes come back wrapped in a list: `getAttr("box.translate")` is `[(x, y, z)]`. Use `[0]` to get the tuple.
Multi attributes can have gaps. Use `multiIndices=True` instead of assuming indices 0 to size-1.
`worldMatrix` is an array attribute (one entry per instance). Ask for `worldMatrix[0]`.
Reading a message attribute raises an error because it has no value. Use `listConnections` instead.

examples.title: Group objects under a new transform
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polySphere(name="b")[0]
grp = cmds.group(a, b, name="geo_grp")

print(grp)  # 'geo_grp'
print(cmds.listRelatives(grp, children=True))  # ['a', 'b']

examples.title: Empty groups for a rig hierarchy
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

root = cmds.group(empty=True, name="rig")
for name in ("geo", "skeleton", "controls"):
    cmds.group(empty=True, name=name, parent=root)
print(cmds.listRelatives(root, children=True))  # ['geo', 'skeleton', 'controls']

examples.title: Offset group above a control (zero out its values)
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="hand_ctrl")[0]
cmds.xform(ctrl, worldSpace=True, translation=(5, 3, 0), rotation=(0, 0, 30))

offset = cmds.group(empty=True, name="hand_ctrl_offset")
cmds.matchTransform(offset, ctrl)
cmds.parent(ctrl, offset)
cmds.xform(ctrl, translation=(0, 0, 0), rotation=(0, 0, 0))

print(cmds.getAttr(ctrl + ".translate"))  # [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(ctrl, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)])  # [5.0, 3.0, 0.0]

gotchas: `group()` with no objects and no `empty=True` groups the current selection.
The group's pivot is at the world origin by default, not the center of its children. Use `xform(grp, centerPivots=True)` if needed.

examples.title: Two-bone IK with a pole vector
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
shoulder = cmds.joint(name="shoulder", position=(0, 0, 0))
elbow = cmds.joint(name="elbow", position=(5, 0, -1))
wrist = cmds.joint(name="wrist", position=(10, 0, 0))

handle, effector = cmds.ikHandle(startJoint=shoulder, endEffector=wrist, solver="ikRPsolver", name="arm_ik")
pole = cmds.spaceLocator(name="arm_pole")[0]
cmds.xform(pole, worldSpace=True, translation=(5, 0, -10))
cmds.poleVectorConstraint(pole, handle)

cmds.xform(handle, worldSpace=True, translation=(8, 2, 0))
wrist_pos = cmds.xform(wrist, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)
print([round(v, 2) for v in wrist_pos])  # [8.0, 2.0, 0.0]
print(cmds.ikHandle(handle, query=True, jointList=True))  # ['shoulder', 'elbow']

examples.title: Spline IK along a curve
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
joints = [cmds.joint(name="tail%d" % i, position=(0, 0, i * 2)) for i in range(5)]
curve = cmds.curve(name="tailCurve", degree=3, point=[(0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 3), (0, 0, 5), (0, 0, 8)])

handle = cmds.ikHandle(startJoint=joints[0], endEffector=joints[-1], curve=curve, solver="ikSplineSolver",
                       createCurve=False, parentCurve=False, name="tail_ik")[0]
print(cmds.nodeType(cmds.ikHandle(handle, query=True, solver=True)))  # 'ikSplineSolver'

examples.title: Turn IK off and on
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
a = cmds.joint(name="a")
b = cmds.joint(name="b", position=(0, 5, 0))
handle = cmds.ikHandle(startJoint=a, endEffector=b)[0]

cmds.setAttr(handle + ".ikBlend", 0)  # FK
print(cmds.getAttr(handle + ".ikBlend"))  # 0.0

gotchas: The rotate-plane solver needs a small bend in the chain at creation; a perfectly straight chain can't decide which way to bend.
Moving the handle doesn't update joint values until the scene evaluates; query world positions with `xform` after setting it.
For spline IK with an existing curve, pass `createCurve=False` or Maya builds a new curve.
Use `ikBlend` on the handle to switch between IK and FK.

examples.title: Build a chain from positions
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
positions = [(0, 0, 0), (0, 5, 0), (0, 10, 1)]
chain = [cmds.joint(name="spine%d" % i, position=p) for i, p in enumerate(positions)]

print(chain)  # ['spine0', 'spine1', 'spine2']
print(cmds.listRelatives("spine2", parent=True))  # ['spine1']
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform("spine2", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)])  # [0.0, 10.0, 1.0]

examples.title: Orient joints so X points down the chain
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
cmds.joint(name="arm", position=(0, 0, 0))
cmds.joint(name="elbow", position=(5, 0, -1))
cmds.joint(name="wrist", position=(10, 0, 0))

examples.title: Start a new chain instead of continuing the last one
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
cmds.joint(name="left_hip")
cmds.joint(name="left_knee", position=(0, -5, 0))

cmds.select(clear=True)  # without this the next joint parents under left_knee
right = cmds.joint(name="right_hip", position=(2, 0, 0))
print(cmds.listRelatives(right, parent=True))  # None

examples.title: Radius and rotation limits
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
knee = cmds.joint(name="knee", radius=2)
cmds.joint(knee, edit=True, limitSwitchZ=True, limitZ=(-150, 0))

print(cmds.joint(knee, query=True, radius=True))  # [2.0]
print(cmds.transformLimits(knee, query=True, rotationZ=True))  # [-150.0, 0.0]

gotchas: New joints are parented under the selected joint. Call `cmds.select(clear=True)` before starting a new chain.
`position` is in world space by default, even when the joint gets a parent.
Orient with `orientJoint`, and set the end joint to `"none"` so it doesn't get an arbitrary orientation.
Rotation values and joint orient are separate: keep `rotate` at zero in the bind pose and put the orientation in `jointOrient`.

summary: Sets and queries tangents on animation curve keys: type, angle, weight and locking.
returns: With `query`, a list of tangent values per key.

flags.outTangentType: Type of the out-tangent. Same values as `inTangentType`.
flags.commonTangentValue: Query only: the tangent value shared by all selected keys.
flags.inTangentType: Type of the in-tangent: `"auto"`, `"spline"`, `"linear"`, `"flat"`, `"step"`, `"stepnext"`, `"fixed"`, `"clamped"`, `"plateau"` or a plug-in type.

flags.outAngle: Angle of the out-tangent in degrees.
flags.inAngle: Angle of the in-tangent in degrees.
flags.lock: Lock the in- and out-tangents together, so they move as one.
flags.relative: Add to the current angles and weights instead of replacing them.
flags.inWeight: Weight of the in-tangent. Only for curves with weighted tangents.
flags.absolute: Set angles and weights as absolute values. This is the default.
flags.pluginTangentTypes: Query only: tangent types added by plug-ins.
flags.stepAttributes: Use step tangents for attributes that can't interpolate, such as booleans and enums.
flags.outWeight: Weight of the out-tangent. Only for curves with weighted tangents.
flags.global: Set the default tangent types for new keys.
flags.weightLock: Lock the tangent weights so only the angles can change.
flags.weightedTangents: Turn weighted tangents on or off for the whole curve.
flags.controlPoints: Also include curves on the objects' control points (vertices, CVs).
flags.time: Time range to use: a single time or `(start, end)`. In MEL, `"start:end"`.
flags.float: Range of float inputs for curves not driven by time, such as driven keys: a single value or `(start, end)`.
flags.animation: Which curves to work on: `"objects"` (all curves on the given objects), `"keys"` (selected keys) or `"keysOrObjects"` (selected keys if any, else the objects). In query mode it takes a boolean.
flags.index: Range of key indices (0-based): a single index or `(start, end)`.

examples.title: Make all keys linear
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
for t, v in ((1, 0), (10, 10), (20, 0)):
    cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=t, value=v)

cmds.keyTangent(box, attribute="translateY", inTangentType="linear", outTangentType="linear")
print(cmds.keyTangent(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, outTangentType=True))  # ['linear', 'linear', 'linear']

examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.keyTangent(g=True, inTangentType="linear", outTangentType="step")
print(cmds.keyTangent(query=True, g=True, outTangentType=True))  # ['step']
cmds.keyTangent(g=True, inTangentType="auto", outTangentType="auto")

examples.title: Flat tangents on one key
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
for t, v in ((1, 0), (10, 10), (20, 0)):
    cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=t, value=v)

cmds.keyTangent(box, attribute="translateY", time=(10, 10), inTangentType="flat", outTangentType="flat")
print(cmds.keyTangent(box, attribute="translateY", time=(10, 10), query=True, outAngle=True))  # [0.0]

gotchas: `global` is a reserved word in Python, so pass the short flag instead: `cmds.keyTangent(g=True, ...)`.
Tangent types apply to keys in the `time` range; without it, all keys on the curve change.
`step` is only valid as an out tangent; the in tangent of the next key doesn't matter for stepped curves.

examples.title: Read key times and values
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
for t, v in ((1, 0), (10, 5), (20, 0)):
    cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=t, value=v)

times = cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, timeChange=True)
values = cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, valueChange=True)
print(list(zip(times, values)))  # [(1.0, 0.0), (10.0, 5.0), (20.0, 0.0)]
print(cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, keyframeCount=True))  # 3

examples.title: First and last key of an object
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateX", time=5)
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="rotateY", time=48)

times = cmds.keyframe(box, query=True, timeChange=True)
print(min(times), max(times))  # (5.0, 48.0)
print(cmds.findKeyframe(box, which="last"))  # 48.0

examples.title: Shift animation in time and value
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=1, value=0)
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=10, value=5)

cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", edit=True, relative=True, timeChange=10)
cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", edit=True, relative=True, valueChange=2, time=(20, 20))
print(cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, timeChange=True))  # [11.0, 20.0]
print(cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, valueChange=True))  # [0.0, 7.0]

examples.title: Evaluate a curve between keys
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=1, value=0, outTangentType="linear")
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=11, value=10, inTangentType="linear")

print([round(v, 6) for v in cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, eval=True, time=(6, 6))])  # [5.0]

examples.title: Animation curve names
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute=["translateX", "rotateZ"], time=1)
print(sorted(cmds.keyframe(box, query=True, name=True)))  # ['box_rotateZ', 'box_translateX']

gotchas: `time=(a, b)` is a range, including the end by default. For a single key in Python pass `time=(t, t)`.
`timeChange` and `valueChange` in query mode return lists; with edits they set, or with `relative=True` offset, the values.
Queries on an object without animation return `None`, not an empty list.
In query mode `animation` takes a boolean, while in edit mode it takes `"objects"`, `"keys"` or `"keysOrObjects"`.

examples.title: Keyable and user-defined attributes
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
cmds.addAttr(ctrl, longName="stretch", attributeType="double", keyable=True)

print(cmds.listAttr(ctrl, userDefined=True))  # ['stretch']
print(cmds.listAttr(ctrl, keyable=True))  # ['visibility', 'translateX', 'translateY', 'translateZ', 'rotateX', 'rotateY', 'rotateZ', 'scaleX', 'scaleY', 'scaleZ', 'stretch']

examples.title: Locked attributes
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setAttr(box + ".tx", lock=True)
cmds.setAttr(box + ".ry", lock=True)
print(cmds.listAttr(box, locked=True))  # ['translateX', 'rotateY']

examples.title: Filter by name
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
print(cmds.listAttr(box, string="scale?"))  # ['scaleX', 'scaleY', 'scaleZ']

examples.title: Copy keyable values between objects
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polyCube(name="b")[0]
cmds.setAttr(a + ".translate", 1, 2, 3)

for attr in cmds.listAttr(a, keyable=True, scalar=True) or []:
    if cmds.getAttr("%s.%s" % (b, attr), settable=True):
        cmds.setAttr("%s.%s" % (b, attr), cmds.getAttr("%s.%s" % (a, attr)))
print(cmds.getAttr(b + ".translate"))  # [(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)]

gotchas: Without flags, `listAttr` returns hundreds of attributes, including internal ones. Filter with `keyable`, `userDefined`, `channelBox` or `string`.
Returns `None` when nothing matches.
Multi attributes are listed without indices unless you use `multi=True`, and aliases replace names (e.g. blend shape weights).

examples.title: Incoming and outgoing connections
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(ctrl + ".translateY", box + ".translateY")

print(cmds.listConnections(box, source=True, destination=False))  # ['ctrl']
print(cmds.listConnections(ctrl, source=False, destination=True))  # ['box']

examples.title: Plug pairs: which attribute connects to which
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(ctrl + ".rotateY", box + ".rotateY")

pairs = cmds.listConnections(box, source=True, destination=False, plugs=True, connections=True)
print(pairs)  # ['box.rotateY', 'ctrl.rotateY']
for dst, src in zip(pairs[::2], pairs[1::2]):
    print(src + " -> " + dst)  # 'ctrl.rotateY -> box.rotateY'

examples.title: Find the skinCluster of a mesh
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
jnt = cmds.joint(name="jnt")
cmds.select(clear=True)
mesh = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
skin = cmds.skinCluster(jnt, mesh, name="boxSkin")[0]

shape = cmds.listRelatives(mesh, shapes=True, noIntermediate=True)[0]
print(cmds.listConnections(shape, type="skinCluster"))  # ['boxSkin']
print(cmds.ls(cmds.listHistory(shape), type="skinCluster"))  # ['boxSkin']  (also finds deformers further up the chain)

examples.title: Look past unit conversion nodes
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(ctrl + ".rotateY", box + ".translateX")  # angle -> distance

print(cmds.nodeType(cmds.listConnections(box + ".translateX")[0]))  # 'unitConversion'
print(cmds.listConnections(box + ".translateX", skipConversionNodes=True))  # ['ctrl']

examples.title: Animation curves on an object
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute=["translateX", "rotateY"], time=1)

print(sorted(cmds.listConnections(box, type="animCurve")))  # ['box_rotateY', 'box_translateX']

gotchas: Nothing connected returns `None`. Write `cmds.listConnections(node) or []` before looping.
Both directions are listed by default. Pass `source=True, destination=False` (or the reverse) to get only one.
Connections from a shape are reported as its transform unless you pass `shapes=True`.

`listConnections(shape, type="skinCluster")` only finds the last deformer, which connects straight to the shape. When other deformers sit on top, use `cmds.ls(cmds.listHistory(shape), type="skinCluster")`.
Unit conversion nodes appear between attributes of different units. Pass `skipConversionNodes=True` to see the real node.

cmds.polyExtrudeFacet(box + ".f[1]", localTranslateZ=1)
print([cmds.nodeType(n) for n in cmds.listHistory(box)])  # ['mesh', 'polyExtrudeFace', 'polyCube']

examples.title: Deformers on a mesh
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.cluster(box, name="c1")
cmds.nonLinear(box, type="bend", name="bend")

deformers = cmds.ls(cmds.listHistory(box, pruneDagObjects=True), type="geometryFilter")
print(sorted(deformers))  # ['bend', 'c1']

examples.title: What depends on a node (future)
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
ctrl = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
cmds.connectAttr(ctrl + ".translateY", box + ".translateY")

print(cmds.listHistory(ctrl, future=True))  # ['ctrlShape']  (a transform follows its shape)
print(cmds.listHistory(ctrl + ".translateY", future=True))  # ['ctrl', 'box']
print(cmds.listHistory("polyCube1", future=True))  # ['polyCube1', 'boxShape']

gotchas: The object itself (or its shape) is the first item. Filter with `pruneDagObjects=True` or `ls(..., type=...)`.
On a transform, history and future come from its shape. To see what a control's attributes drive, pass the plug: `listHistory("ctrl.translateY", future=True)`.
Deformers share the base type `geometryFilter`, so `ls(history, type="geometryFilter")` finds all of them.
History can be long in big scenes; `levels=` limits how far it goes.

listNodeTypes.name: listNodeTypes
summary: Lists node types by classification, e.g. `"shader/surface"` or `"texture/2D"`.

flags.exclude: Leave out types with this classification.

listNodesWithIncorrectNames.name: listNodesWithIncorrectNames
summary: Lists nodes whose names aren't valid.

listRelatives.name: listRelatives
summary: Lists DAG relatives of the given objects: children, descendants, parents or shapes. With no objects passed it uses the current selection, and with no relationship flag it lists direct children.
returns: A list of node names, or `None` when nothing matches (not an empty list). Raises `ValueError` if an object you pass does not exist.

flags.children: Direct children only. This is the default when none of `children`, `allDescendents`, `parent`, `allParents` or `shapes` is given.
flags.allDescendents: Every node below the object at any depth, including shapes. A node's descendants are listed before the node itself, so reverse the list if you need top-down order.
flags.parent: The direct parent. Returns `None` for nodes that sit directly under the world. On a shape it returns the owning transform.
flags.allParents: Every direct parent of an instanced node, one per instance. It does **not** walk up to ancestors; for a non-instanced node it gives the same result as `parent`.
flags.shapes: Shape nodes directly under the given transforms. It always looks only one level down, even when combined with `children` or `allDescendents`.
flags.fullPath: Return full DAG paths starting with `|`. These are always unique, so use this whenever the result is passed to another command. Wins over `path` if both are set.
flags.path: Return the shortest path that is unique in the scene, which is the plain name when no other node shares it.
flags.noIntermediate: Skip intermediate objects, such as the hidden `…ShapeOrig` shape a deformer creates.
flags.type: Only return nodes of this type or a type derived from it, so abstract types like `shape` or `geometryShape` work. Pass a list to allow several types.

examples.title: Get the shape of a transform
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
shapes = cmds.listRelatives(cube, shapes=True, noIntermediate=True, fullPath=True) or []
print(shapes)  # ['|box|boxShape']

examples.title: Skip deformer "Orig" shapes
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

tube = cmds.polyCylinder(name="tube")[0]
cmds.cluster(tube)

print(cmds.listRelatives(tube, shapes=True))  # ['tubeShape', 'tubeShapeOrig']
print(cmds.listRelatives(tube, shapes=True, noIntermediate=True))  # ['tubeShape']

examples.title: Every mesh under a group
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

rig = cmds.group(empty=True, name="rig")
cmds.parent(cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0], rig)
sub = cmds.group(empty=True, name="sub", parent=rig)
cmds.parent(cmds.polySphere(name="ball")[0], sub)

meshes = cmds.listRelatives(rig, allDescendents=True, type="mesh", noIntermediate=True, fullPath=True) or []
print(meshes)  # ['|rig|box|boxShape', '|rig|sub|ball|ballShape']

from maya import cmds

examples.title: Ancestors (not `allParents`)
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

rig = cmds.group(empty=True, name="rig")
sub = cmds.group(empty=True, name="sub", parent=rig)
ball = cmds.polySphere(name="ball")[0]
ball = cmds.parent(ball, sub)[0]

print(cmds.listRelatives(ball, allParents=True))  # ['sub']

long_name = cmds.ls(ball, long=True)[0]
ancestors = long_name.split("|")[1:-1]
print(ancestors)  # ['rig', 'sub']

items.name: ls
items.text: `cmds.ls(root, dag=True, type="mesh", noIntermediate=True, long=True)` also searches a whole hierarchy, but it includes `root` itself and lists top-down. It's also how you get long names for ancestors: `cmds.ls(node, long=True)`.

items.name: objExists
items.text: Check a name before passing it in, since `listRelatives` raises on a missing object instead of returning `None`.

items.name: nodeType
items.text: Exact type of each result, e.g. `mesh` vs `nurbsCurve`.

items.name: objectType
items.text: `cmds.objectType(node, isAType="shape")` tests against a base type, matching how the `type` flag filters.

items.name: parent
items.text: Reparent nodes, or move them to the world with `world=True`. It returns the new names, which you should use instead of the old ones.

items.name: group
items.text: Create an empty transform to parent results under.

items.name: listConnections
items.text: Relatives in the dependency graph rather than the hierarchy, e.g. `cmds.listConnections(shape, type="skinCluster")`.

items.name: listHistory
items.text: Everything upstream of a shape. It has no `type` flag, so filter it: `cmds.ls(cmds.listHistory(shape), type="skinCluster")`.

items.name: MDagPath
items.text: `childCount()`, `child()`, `extendToShape()` and `fullPathName()`, with no string name lookups.

items.name: MFnDagNode
items.text: `parent()`, `child()` and `instanceCount()` for walking and instancing on a node.

items.name: MItDag
items.text: Fast depth- or breadth-first iteration over large hierarchies, where many `listRelatives` calls get slow.

gotchas: Nothing found returns `None`, so `for child in cmds.listRelatives(node):` raises `TypeError`. Write `cmds.listRelatives(node) or []`.
Without `fullPath` (or `path`) you get plain names even when they are ambiguous: if two nodes are called `box`, passing the result back into a command fails with "More than one object matches name".
`shapes=True, allDescendents=True` does not find shapes deeper in the hierarchy. Use `allDescendents=True, type="shape"` (or `type="mesh"`) instead.
Deformed meshes have an extra intermediate shape. Add `noIntermediate=True` whenever you want the shape you see in the viewport.
`allParents` is about instancing, not ancestry. Split the long name from `cmds.ls(node, long=True)` to get ancestors.

summary: Locks nodes so they can't be deleted, renamed or reparented.

loft.name: loft
summary: Creates a surface through a series of curves.

flags.autoReverse: Reverse curves automatically so they all point the same way.
flags.createCusp: Make a sharp edge at this curve. Repeat once per curve.
flags.sectionSpans: Number of spans between each pair of curves.
flags.degree: Degree in the loft direction: 1 linear, 3 cubic.
flags.close: Close the surface by joining the last curve back to the first.
flags.reverse: Reverse this curve's direction. Repeat once per curve.
flags.name: Name for the created object or node.
flags.object: Create the result object. When off, only the dependency node is created.
flags.nodeState: Set the node's state: 0 normal, 1 has no effect (passes input through), 2 blocking.
flags.constructionHistory: Keep construction history. When on, a node is created that you can edit later; when off, the result is baked and no history node remains.
flags.frozen: Set the node's frozen attribute. A frozen node stops evaluating and keeps its last output.
flags.caching: Set the node's caching attribute. When on, the node keeps its output so it doesn't have to recompute.

lookThru.name: lookThru
summary: Makes a panel look through a camera or light.

ls.name: ls
summary: Lists nodes in the scene: by name pattern, type, selection and many other filters.
returns: A list of names, always a list (empty when nothing matches, unlike `listRelatives`).

flags.undeletable: Only list nodes that can't be deleted.
flags.invisible: Only list objects that aren't visible, including ones hidden by a parent or layer.
flags.objectsOnly: For components and attributes, return only the object names without the component or attribute part.
flags.defaultNodes: List Maya's default nodes, such as `time1` and `lambert1`.
flags.long: Return full DAG paths, which are always unique.
flags.type: Only list nodes of this type or a derived type. Can be repeated.
flags.absoluteName: Return names including the full namespace path with a leading `:`.
flags.referencedNodes: Only list nodes that come from referenced files.
flags.recursive: With namespaces in the pattern, search all child namespaces too.
flags.live: List objects that are made live for snapping.
flags.exactType: Only list nodes of exactly this type, not types derived from it.
flags.orderedSelection: Return selected objects in the order they were selected.
flags.containerType: With `containers`, only list containers of this type, e.g. `"asset"`.
flags.allPaths: Return every DAG path to instanced objects instead of only the first.
flags.ghost: List ghosting nodes used for animation ghosts.
flags.dependencyNodes: List dependency graph nodes, including DAG nodes.
flags.dagObjects: List DAG nodes. With names, also lists everything below them.
flags.persistentNodes: List nodes that Maya keeps across new scenes.
flags.geometry: List geometry shapes, such as meshes, curves and surfaces.
flags.uuid: Return node UUIDs instead of names. Names passed in can also be UUIDs.
flags.head: Return only the first N results. With some filter flags it's applied before filtering, so it can return fewer items than expected.
flags.leaf: With `dagObjects`, only list leaf nodes (nodes without children).
flags.showType: Return the type of each result after its name.
flags.excludeType: Leave out nodes of this type and derived types.
flags.shortNames: Return short names, even if they're not unique.
flags.untemplated: Only list objects that aren't templated.
flags.preSelectHilite: List components highlighted by pre-selection (under the cursor).
flags.flatten: List every component on its own, e.g. `pCube1.vtx[0]`, `pCube1.vtx[1]` instead of `pCube1.vtx[0:7]`.
flags.showNamespace: Return the namespace of each result after its name.
flags.intermediateObjects: Only list intermediate objects, such as the `…ShapeOrig` shapes deformers create.
flags.hilite: List objects that are highlighted for component editing.
flags.readOnly: Only list read-only nodes, such as those from references.
flags.orderedComponentSelection: Return selected components in the order they were selected. Requires "Track selection order" to be on.
flags.ufeObjects: Return UFE paths for non-Maya objects, such as USD prims in the selection.
flags.assemblies: List top-level DAG nodes, the direct children of the world.
flags.nodeTypes: Return the names of all node types in Maya instead of nodes.
flags.tail: Return only the last N results.
flags.modified: Only list nodes that were changed since the file was loaded or saved.

from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polySphere(name="b")[0]
cmds.select(b, a)

print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['b', 'a']
print(cmds.ls(selection=True, long=True))  # ['|b', '|a']

    cmds.circle(name=name)
cmds.joint(name="L_arm_jnt")

print(sorted(cmds.ls("L_*_ctrl")))  # ['L_arm_ctrl', 'L_leg_ctrl']

rig = cmds.group(empty=True, name="rig")

examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.select(cube + ".vtx[0:2]")

print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['box.vtx[0:2]']
print(cmds.ls(selection=True, flatten=True))  # ['box.vtx[0]', 'box.vtx[1]', 'box.vtx[2]']

examples.title: Search namespaces and get UUIDs
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.namespace(add="char")
cmds.polyCube(name="char:body")
cmds.polyCube(name="body")

print(sorted(cmds.ls("*:body")))  # ['char:body']
print(sorted(cmds.ls("body", recursive=True)))  # ['body', 'char:body']

uuid = cmds.ls("char:body", uuid=True)[0]
print(cmds.ls(uuid))  # ['char:body']

gotchas: Component selections come back as ranges like `box.vtx[0:7]`. Use `flatten=True` to iterate one component at a time.
`type="mesh"` includes intermediate `…ShapeOrig` shapes on deformed meshes. Add `noIntermediate=True`.
Plain `*` doesn't search inside namespaces. Use `*:name`, or `recursive=True`.
Short names are only unique if no other node shares them. Use `long=True` when passing results to other commands.
A UUID survives renames, so `cmds.ls(uuid=True)` is a safe way to remember a node across a script.

makeIdentity.name: makeIdentity
summary: Freezes transformations: resets translate, rotate and scale to identity while keeping objects in place, or resets them.
returns: Nothing.

flags.jointOrient: For joints, move rotation into the joint orient.
flags.preserveNormals: Keep normals facing the same way for negatively scaled objects.
flags.normal: How normals are handled: 0 unchanged, 1 frozen, 2 unfrozen after freezing.
flags.apply: Bake the transform into the geometry (and child transforms) before resetting it. Off just resets values and the object moves.

examples.title: Freeze transformations
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.xform(box, translation=(1, 2, 3), rotation=(0, 45, 0), scale=(2, 2, 2))
before = [round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(box + ".vtx[0]", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)]

cmds.makeIdentity(box, apply=True, translate=True, rotate=True, scale=True)
print(cmds.getAttr(box + ".translate"))  # [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]
print(cmds.getAttr(box + ".scale"))  # [(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)]
after = [round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(box + ".vtx[0]", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)]
print(after == before)  # True  (the geometry didn't move)

examples.title: Freeze only scale
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.xform(box, translation=(5, 0, 0), scale=(3, 3, 3))

cmds.makeIdentity(box, apply=True, scale=True)
print(cmds.getAttr(box + ".translateX"))  # 5.0
print(cmds.getAttr(box + ".scale"))  # [(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)]

examples.title: Move joint rotations into joint orient
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
jnt = cmds.joint(name="jnt")
cmds.setAttr(jnt + ".rotate", 0, 30, 0)

cmds.makeIdentity(jnt, apply=True, rotate=True)
print(cmds.getAttr(jnt + ".rotate"))  # [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.getAttr(jnt + ".jointOrient")[0]])  # [0.0, 30.0, 0.0]

gotchas: Without `apply=True`, the values are just reset to zero/one and the object moves.
Freezing translation moves pivots to world space values, so the rotate pivot is no longer at the origin of the object.
Freezing fails on objects with incoming connections or locked channels.
On a skinned mesh, freeze before binding. Freezing afterwards is blocked by the history.

matchTransform.name: matchTransform
summary: Moves, rotates and scales objects to match a target object.
returns: Nothing.

flags.scaleBox: Scale to match the target's bounding box.

examples.title: Snap position and rotation to a target
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.xform(target, worldSpace=True, translation=(3, 4, 5), rotation=(0, 90, 0))
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

cmds.matchTransform(obj, target)
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(obj, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)])  # [3.0, 4.0, 5.0]
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(obj, query=True, worldSpace=True, rotation=True)])  # [0.0, 90.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Match only position
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.xform(target, worldSpace=True, translation=(1, 1, 1), rotation=(45, 0, 0))
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

cmds.matchTransform(obj, target, position=True)
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.getAttr(obj + ".translate")[0]])  # [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
print(cmds.getAttr(obj + ".rotate"))  # [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]

examples.title: Works through parent transforms
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
cmds.xform(grp, translation=(10, 0, 0), rotation=(0, 45, 0))
obj = cmds.parent(cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0], grp)[0]
target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.xform(target, worldSpace=True, translation=(0, 5, 0))

cmds.matchTransform(obj, target, position=True)
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(obj, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)])  # [0.0, 5.0, 0.0]

gotchas: With no attribute flags, position, rotation and scale are all matched.
It matches world space pivots; if pivots differ from the object origin, results differ from snapping translate values.

examples.title: Create a namespace and work inside it
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.namespace(add="char01")
cmds.namespace(setNamespace="char01")
box = cmds.polyCube(name="body")[0]
cmds.namespace(setNamespace=":")

print(box)  # 'char01:body'
print(cmds.namespace(exists="char01"))  # True

examples.title: List nodes in a namespace
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.namespace(add="prop")
cmds.polyCube(name="prop:box")
cmds.polySphere(name="prop:ball")

nodes = cmds.namespaceInfo("prop", listNamespace=True)
print(sorted(n for n in nodes if cmds.nodeType(n) == "transform"))  # ['prop:ball', 'prop:box']

examples.title: Remove a namespace and keep its contents
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.namespace(add="temp")
cmds.polyCube(name="temp:box")

cmds.namespace(removeNamespace="temp", mergeNamespaceWithRoot=True)
print(cmds.objExists("box"))  # True
print(cmds.namespace(exists="temp"))  # False

examples.title: Rename a namespace
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.namespace(add="old")
cmds.polyCube(name="old:box")
cmds.namespace(rename=("old", "new"))
print(cmds.ls("new:*", type="transform"))  # ['new:box']

gotchas: Always go back to the root with `namespace(setNamespace=":")` after working in a namespace; otherwise later nodes land in it too.
`removeNamespace` fails if the namespace isn't empty, unless you merge (`mergeNamespaceWithRoot=True`) or delete its content (`deleteNamespaceContent=True`).
Namespaces from references can't be removed or renamed this way; use the `file` command on the reference.

from maya import cmds

from maya import cmds

summary: Returns True if an object with the given name exists. Works for nodes, attributes (`node.attr`) and components.
returns: True or False.

examples.title: Nodes, attributes and components
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
print(cmds.objExists("box"))  # True
print(cmds.objExists("box.translateX"))  # True
print(cmds.objExists("box.notAnAttr"))  # False
print(cmds.objExists("box.vtx[7]"))  # True
print(cmds.objExists("box.vtx[100]"))  # True  (component indices aren't checked)
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(box, vertex=True))  # 8

examples.title: Ambiguous short names still "exist"
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.group(empty=True, name="a")
b = cmds.group(empty=True, name="b")
cmds.group(empty=True, name="item", parent=a)
cmds.group(empty=True, name="item", parent=b)

print(cmds.objExists("item"))  # True
print(len(cmds.ls("item")))  # 2

gotchas: `objExists` is True even when a short name matches several nodes, and commands then fail with "More than one object matches name". Use `len(cmds.ls(name)) == 1` when you need a unique match.
Component indices aren't validated: `objExists("box.vtx[100]")` is True on an 8-vertex cube. Compare against `polyEvaluate(mesh, vertex=True)`.
For attributes, `attributeQuery(attr, node=node, exists=True)` is clearer and doesn't depend on name parsing.

examples.title: Store and read tool settings
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.optionVar(stringValue=("myTool_lastPath", "/projects/show"))
cmds.optionVar(intValue=("myTool_count", 3))

print(cmds.optionVar(query="myTool_lastPath"))  # '/projects/show'
print(cmds.optionVar(query="myTool_count"))  # 3

examples.title: Defaults when a setting doesn't exist
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

def get_pref(name, default):
    return cmds.optionVar(query=name) if cmds.optionVar(exists=name) else default

cmds.optionVar(remove="myTool_mode")
print(get_pref("myTool_mode", "fast"))  # 'fast'
print(cmds.optionVar(query="myTool_mode"))  # 0  (missing variables read as 0)

examples.title: Arrays
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.optionVar(clearArray="myTool_recent")
for path in ("a.ma", "b.ma"):
    cmds.optionVar(stringValueAppend=("myTool_recent", path))

print(cmds.optionVar(query="myTool_recent"))  # ['a.ma', 'b.ma']
print(cmds.optionVar(arraySize="myTool_recent"))  # 2

gotchas: Querying a variable that doesn't exist returns `0` instead of failing. Check `exists` first.
Prefix names with your tool name; all tools share one namespace of variables.
Values are written to disk when Maya quits normally or preferences are saved, not immediately.

examples.title: Match a target's orientation
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.setAttr(target + ".rotate", 0, 90, 0)
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

cmds.orientConstraint(target, obj)
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.getAttr(obj + ".rotate")[0]])  # [0.0, 90.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Blend between two orientations
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.spaceLocator(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.spaceLocator(name="b")[0]
cmds.setAttr(b + ".rotateY", 90)
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

con = cmds.orientConstraint(a, b, obj)[0]
print(round(cmds.getAttr(obj + ".rotateY"), 3))  # 45.0

cmds.setAttr(con + ".interpType", 2)  # shortest
print(cmds.getAttr(con + ".interpType", asString=True))  # 'Shortest'

gotchas: Blending orientations can flip when targets are far apart. Set `interpType` (e.g. Shortest or No Flip), or cache the rotation with `createCache`.
The constraint drives `rotate`, so joint orient on joints is taken into account automatically.

flags.position: Query only: position of the locator.

parent.name: parent
summary: Reparents DAG objects: the last argument is the new parent. Returns the objects' new names.
returns: The new names of the objects. Names can change when an object with the same short name exists under the new parent, so always use the returned value.

flags.world: Move the objects under the world.
flags.noConnections: When instancing with `addObject`, don't copy input connections.
flags.shape: Parent a shape node directly under another transform.
flags.addObject: Add another parent (instance the object) instead of moving it.
flags.absolute: Keep the objects' world space position by adjusting their transforms. This is the default.
flags.removeObject: Remove the object from this parent. If it has no other parents, it is deleted.
flags.relative: Keep the objects' local transform values, so they move with the new parent.
flags.noInvScale: Don't connect the parent's scale to a joint's inverse scale.

examples.title: Parent and keep the world position
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
cmds.move(0, 10, 0, grp)
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

box = cmds.parent(box, grp)[0]
print(box)  # 'box'
print(cmds.getAttr(box + ".translateY"))  # -10.0  (local value changed so it stays put)
print(cmds.xform(box, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True))  # [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Parent and keep the local values instead
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
cmds.move(0, 10, 0, grp)
box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

box = cmds.parent(box, grp, relative=True)[0]
print(cmds.getAttr(box + ".translateY"))  # 0.0
print(cmds.xform(box, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True))  # [0.0, 10.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Unparent to the world
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
box = cmds.parent(cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0], grp)[0]

box = cmds.parent(box, world=True)[0]
print(cmds.ls(box, long=True))  # ['|box']

examples.title: Use the returned name after a clash
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.group(empty=True, name="a")
b = cmds.group(empty=True, name="b")
cmds.group(empty=True, name="item", parent=a)
cmds.group(empty=True, name="item", parent=b)

moved = cmds.parent("b|item", a)[0]
print(moved)  # 'item1'
print(sorted(cmds.listRelatives(a, children=True)))  # ['item', 'item1']

examples.title: Put a shape under another transform
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

circle = cmds.circle(name="ctrl")[0]
square = cmds.nurbsSquare(name="square")[0]
curves = cmds.listRelatives(square, allDescendents=True, type="nurbsCurve")

cmds.parent(curves, circle, shape=True, relative=True)
print(len(cmds.listRelatives(circle, shapes=True)))  # 5

gotchas: `parent` keeps the world position by default, so local translate/rotate values change. Use `relative=True` to keep the local values.
Always use the returned names. The object can be renamed if a sibling already has the same name.
Moving a shape needs `shape=True` (and usually `relative=True`), otherwise Maya parents its transform.
Parenting a joint under a joint connects `scale` to `inverseScale`. Pass `noInvScale=True` to skip that.

parentConstraint.name: parentConstraint
summary: Constrains an object's translation and rotation as if it were parented to the targets.
returns: The constraint node name, in a list.

flags.decompRotationToChild: Decompose rotation to the child when the constrained object has a parent.
flags.skipTranslate: Axis not to constrain in translation: `"x"`, `"y"`, `"z"` or `"none"`. Can be repeated.
flags.skipRotate: Axis not to constrain in rotation: `"x"`, `"y"`, `"z"` or `"none"`. Can be repeated.
flags.createCache: Cache the constraint's rotation between two times, to avoid flipping.
flags.layer: Animation layer the constraint is added to.
flags.name: Name for the constraint node.
flags.remove: Remove the given targets from the constraint. The constraint is deleted when no targets remain.
flags.weight: Weight of the targets. Use a separate call per target to give them different weights.
flags.targetList: Query only: the targets of the constraint.
flags.maintainOffset: Keep the constrained object's current offset from the targets.
flags.weightAliasList: Query only: the weight attributes, one per target, in the same order as `targetList`.

examples.title: Follow a target and keep the current offset
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

hand = cmds.spaceLocator(name="hand")[0]
cmds.xform(hand, worldSpace=True, translation=(5, 5, 0))
prop = cmds.polyCube(name="sword")[0]
cmds.xform(prop, worldSpace=True, translation=(6, 5, 0))

con = cmds.parentConstraint(hand, prop, maintainOffset=True)[0]
cmds.xform(hand, worldSpace=True, translation=(5, 8, 0))
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(prop, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)])  # [6.0, 8.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Space switching with target weights
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

world = cmds.spaceLocator(name="world_space")[0]
hand = cmds.spaceLocator(name="hand_space")[0]
cmds.xform(hand, worldSpace=True, translation=(10, 0, 0))
ctrl = cmds.polyCube(name="ctrl")[0]

con = cmds.parentConstraint(world, hand, ctrl)[0]
weights = cmds.parentConstraint(con, query=True, weightAliasList=True)
print(weights)  # ['world_spaceW0', 'hand_spaceW1']

cmds.setAttr("%s.%s" % (con, weights[0]), 1)
cmds.setAttr("%s.%s" % (con, weights[1]), 0)
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(ctrl, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)])  # [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Only translation, and list targets
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.xform(target, worldSpace=True, translation=(1, 2, 3), rotation=(0, 45, 0))
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

con = cmds.parentConstraint(target, obj, skipRotate=["x", "y", "z"])[0]
print(cmds.parentConstraint(con, query=True, targetList=True))  # ['target']
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.getAttr(obj + ".rotate")[0]])  # [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Snap without a lasting constraint
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.xform(target, worldSpace=True, translation=(4, 0, 0), rotation=(0, 90, 0))
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

cmds.delete(cmds.parentConstraint(target, obj))
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.getAttr(obj + ".translate")[0]])  # [4.0, 0.0, 0.0]
print(cmds.listConnections(obj, type="constraint"))  # None

gotchas: Weight attributes are named `<target>W<index>`. Get the real names with `weightAliasList=True` instead of building them.
Without `maintainOffset`, the object jumps to the target.
Constrained channels are connected, so they can't be keyed directly. Bake with `bakeResults`, or use a pairBlend (keying a constrained channel adds one).
`cmds.delete(cmds.parentConstraint(...))` is a quick way to snap an object to a target.

examples.title: Set the playback and animation ranges
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.playbackOptions(animationStartTime=1, animationEndTime=200, minTime=10, maxTime=100)
print(cmds.playbackOptions(query=True, minTime=True))  # 10.0
print(cmds.playbackOptions(query=True, maxTime=True))  # 100.0
print(cmds.playbackOptions(query=True, animationEndTime=True))  # 200.0

examples.title: Fit the range to an object's keys
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateX", time=12)
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateX", time=84)

times = cmds.keyframe(box, query=True, timeChange=True)
cmds.playbackOptions(minTime=min(times), maxTime=max(times))
print(cmds.playbackOptions(query=True, minTime=True), cmds.playbackOptions(query=True, maxTime=True))  # (12.0, 84.0)

examples.title: Real-time playback and looping
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.playbackOptions(playbackSpeed=1, loop="once")
print(cmds.playbackOptions(query=True, loop=True))  # 'once'
print(cmds.playbackOptions(query=True, playbackSpeed=True))  # 1.0

examples.title: Average position of several targets
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.spaceLocator(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.spaceLocator(name="b")[0]
cmds.setAttr(a + ".translate", 0, 0, 0)

examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.spaceLocator(name="a")[0]

cmds.setAttr(target + ".translate", 3, 3, 3)
obj = cmds.spaceLocator(name="obj")[0]
