examples.title: Remove a target
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.spaceLocator(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.spaceLocator(name="b")[0]
obj = cmds.spaceLocator(name="obj")[0]
con = cmds.pointConstraint(a, b, obj)[0]

cmds.pointConstraint(b, obj, remove=True)
print(cmds.pointConstraint(con, query=True, targetList=True))  # ['a']

gotchas: Adding a target to an existing constraint uses the same command: `pointConstraint(newTarget, obj)`.
Weights are relative to each other: weights 1 and 3 put the object 75% toward the second target.
Removing the last target deletes the constraint node.

examples.title: Counts
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(box, vertex=True))  # 8
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(box, face=True))  # 6
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(box, triangle=True))  # 12
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(box, vertex=True, face=True))  # {'vertex': 8, 'face': 6}

examples.title: Shells and bounding box
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polyCube(name="b")[0]
cmds.move(3, 0, 0, b)
merged = cmds.polyUnite(a, b, name="merged", constructionHistory=False)[0]

print(cmds.polyEvaluate(merged, shell=True))  # 2
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(merged, boundingBox=True))  # ((-0.5, 3.5), (-0.5, 0.5), (-0.5, 0.5))

examples.title: Area
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

plane = cmds.polyPlane(name="floor", width=4, height=2, subdivisionsX=1, subdivisionsY=1)[0]
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(plane, area=True))  # 8.0
cmds.scale(2, 1, 1, plane)
print(cmds.polyEvaluate(plane, worldArea=True))  # 16.0

gotchas: `boundingBox` returns `((xmin, xmax), (ymin, ymax), (zmin, zmax))`, a different order from `xform -boundingBox`.
`area` ignores the transform; use `worldArea` for world space.
Several flags at once return a dictionary; a single flag returns a plain value.

examples.title: Faces to vertices
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
verts = cmds.polyListComponentConversion(box + ".f[1]", toVertex=True)
print(verts)  # ['box.vtx[2:5]']
print(len(cmds.ls(verts, flatten=True)))  # 4

examples.title: Only components fully inside the selection
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
faces = cmds.polyListComponentConversion(box + ".vtx[2:5]", toFace=True)
inside = cmds.polyListComponentConversion(box + ".vtx[2:5]", toFace=True, internal=True)
print(len(cmds.ls(faces, flatten=True)))  # 5
print(inside)  # ['box.f[1]']

examples.title: Border edges of a face selection
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

plane = cmds.polyPlane(name="plane", subdivisionsX=2, subdivisionsY=1)[0]
border = cmds.polyListComponentConversion(plane + ".f[0:1]", toEdge=True, border=True)
print(len(cmds.ls(border, flatten=True)))  # 6

examples.title: Whole object to UVs
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
uvs = cmds.polyListComponentConversion(box, toUV=True)
print(len(cmds.ls(uvs, flatten=True)))  # 14

gotchas: Results are ranges; flatten with `ls(result, flatten=True)` to count or loop.
Without `internal=True`, conversion is "touching": vertices to faces gives every face that uses any of the vertices.
Passing the object name converts all of its components.

examples.title: Split a mesh into shells
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polyCube(name="b")[0]
cmds.move(3, 0, 0, b)
merged = cmds.polyUnite(a, b, name="merged", constructionHistory=False)[0]

parts = cmds.polySeparate(merged, constructionHistory=False)
print(len(parts))  # 2
print([cmds.polyEvaluate(p, face=True) for p in parts])  # [6, 6]

gotchas: Fails on a mesh with only one shell.
With history, the pieces are driven by the original; delete history to get independent meshes.
The pieces are grouped under the original transform; unparent them if you need them at the top level.

examples.title: With history, then clean up
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polyCube(name="b")[0]
merged, node = cmds.polyUnite(a, b, name="merged")

print(cmds.nodeType(node))  # 'polyUnite'
print(cmds.objExists("a"), cmds.listRelatives("a", shapes=True))  # (True, None)  (empty leftover transform)

cmds.delete(merged, constructionHistory=True)
print(cmds.objExists("a"))  # False

examples.title: Cancellable progress for a long loop
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

items = cmds.ls(type="mesh")
cmds.progressWindow(title="Processing", progress=0, maxValue=max(len(items), 1),
                    status="Starting", isInterruptable=True)
try:
    for i, shape in enumerate(items):
        if cmds.progressWindow(query=True, isCancelled=True):
            break
        cmds.progressWindow(edit=True, progress=i + 1, status=shape)
        # ... work on shape ...
finally:
    cmds.progressWindow(endProgress=True)

gotchas: Always call `endProgress=True` in a `finally` block; a left-over progress window blocks the UI.
Only one progress window can exist at a time.
The window only redraws when Maya processes events; very tight loops may look frozen.

rename.name: rename
summary: Renames a node. Returns the new name, which can differ from the one asked for if it wasn't unique.
returns: The actual new name, which may have a number added if the name was taken.

flags.uuid: Treat the first argument as a node UUID instead of a name.
flags.ignoreShape: Don't rename the transform's shape along with it. By default a shape named after its transform is renamed too.

examples.title: The shape follows the transform
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="pCube1")[0]
new = cmds.rename(box, "hero_geo")
print(new)  # 'hero_geo'
print(cmds.listRelatives(new, shapes=True))  # ['hero_geoShape']

examples.title: Add a prefix to the selection safely
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

for name in ("arm", "leg"):
    cmds.group(empty=True, name=name)
cmds.select("arm", "leg")

uuids = cmds.ls(selection=True, uuid=True)
for uuid in uuids:
    old = cmds.ls(uuid)[0]
    cmds.rename(old, "L_" + old)
print(sorted(cmds.ls(uuids)))  # ['L_arm', 'L_leg']

examples.title: Name clashes get a number
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.group(empty=True, name="ctrl")
other = cmds.group(empty=True, name="temp")
print(cmds.rename(other, "ctrl"))  # 'ctrl1'

examples.title: Search and replace in names

gotchas: Renaming a parent changes the long names of all its children. Store UUIDs (`ls(uuid=True)`) instead of names when renaming in a loop.
A shape is only renamed with its transform if its name matches the transform's pattern (e.g. `boxShape`). Use `ignoreShape=True` to prevent that.
Use the returned name: Maya adds a number when the name exists.

examples.title: Update when the selection changes, tied to a window
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

if cmds.window("selWatcher", exists=True):
    cmds.deleteUI("selWatcher")
win = cmds.window("selWatcher", title="Selection")
cmds.columnLayout(adjustableColumn=True)
label = cmds.text(label="")

def update(*_):
    cmds.text(label, edit=True, label=", ".join(cmds.ls(selection=True)) or "(nothing)")

cmds.scriptJob(event=["SelectionChanged", update], parent=win)
update()
cmds.showWindow(win)

examples.title: Watch an attribute and clean up
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
job = cmds.scriptJob(attributeChange=[box + ".translateY", lambda: print("moved")], killWithScene=True)

print(cmds.scriptJob(exists=job))
cmds.scriptJob(kill=job, force=True)

gotchas: Jobs run when Maya is idle after the change, not immediately, so they don't fire inside a running script and don't run in `mayapy` batch sessions.
Always tie jobs to a UI element (`parent=`) or scene (`killWithScene=True`), or keep the number and kill it. Leaked jobs pile up.
`listEvents=True` and `listConditions=True` show what you can listen to.
For precise, synchronous callbacks use the API's `MNodeMessage`/`MEventMessage`.

examples.title: Replace, add, remove, clear
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a, b, c = [cmds.polyCube(name=n)[0] for n in ("a", "b", "c")]
cmds.select(a)
cmds.select(b, add=True)
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['a', 'b']

cmds.select(a, deselect=True)
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['b']

cmds.select(clear=True)
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # []

examples.title: Select components
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.select(box + ".f[0:1]", box + ".vtx[7]")
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['box.f[0:1]', 'box.vtx[7]']

examples.title: Select a hierarchy
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

rig = cmds.group(empty=True, name="rig")
cmds.parent(cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0], rig)
cmds.select(rig, hierarchy=True)
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['rig', 'box', 'boxShape']

examples.title: Selecting nothing clears the selection
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.polyCube(name="box")
cmds.select("box")
cmds.select(cmds.ls("missing_*"))  # empty list
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # []

examples.title: Keep and restore the user's selection
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

a = cmds.polyCube(name="a")[0]
b = cmds.polyCube(name="b")[0]
cmds.select(a, b)

saved = cmds.ls(selection=True, long=True)
cmds.select(clear=True)
# ... work that changes the selection ...
cmds.select(saved)
print(cmds.ls(selection=True))  # ['a', 'b']

gotchas: `cmds.select([])` clears the selection, which can surprise you when a list comes back empty. Guard with `if nodes:`.
Selecting a set selects its members unless you pass `noExpand=True`.
Most commands work on explicit names; avoid depending on the selection in tools. If you must, save and restore it.

examples.code:

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setAttr(cube + ".translateY", 5)

examples.title: Insert a key without changing the curve
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

box = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=1, value=0)
cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=21, value=20)
before = cmds.getAttr(box + ".translateY", time=15)

cmds.setKeyframe(box, attribute="translateY", time=10, insert=True)
print(cmds.keyframe(box, attribute="translateY", query=True, keyframeCount=True))  # 3
print(round(cmds.getAttr(box + ".translateY", time=15) - before, 6))  # 0.0

gotchas: Without `attribute`, every keyable attribute gets a key, which creates lots of curves. Pass the attributes you mean.
Without `value`, the current value is keyed; without `time`, the current time. In scripts, pass both to avoid depending on scene state.
Default tangents come from preferences, so results can differ between machines. Set `inTangentType` and `outTangentType` when it matters.

Querying by `attribute=` on a transform can also match the shape's attribute of the same name (e.g. `visibility`), returning duplicate values. Query the plug directly: `keyframe("box.visibility", query=True, ...)`.
Keys on `visibility` and other boolean or enum attributes are stepped automatically.

examples.title: Bind a mesh to joints
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
root = cmds.joint(name="root", position=(0, 0, 0))
tip = cmds.joint(name="tip", position=(0, 4, 0))
mesh = cmds.polyCylinder(name="tube", height=4, subdivisionsHeight=4)[0]
cmds.move(0, 2, 0, mesh)

skin = cmds.skinCluster([root, tip], mesh, toSelectedBones=True, maximumInfluences=2, name="tube_skin")[0]
print(skin)  # 'tube_skin'
print(cmds.skinCluster(skin, query=True, influence=True))  # ['root', 'tip']
print(cmds.skinCluster(skin, query=True, maximumInfluences=True))  # 2

examples.title: Find the skinCluster on a mesh
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
jnt = cmds.joint(name="jnt")
mesh = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.skinCluster(jnt, mesh, toSelectedBones=True, name="box_skin")

def find_skin(node):
    history = cmds.listHistory(node, pruneDagObjects=True) or []
    skins = cmds.ls(history, type="skinCluster")
    return skins[0] if skins else None

print(find_skin(mesh))  # 'box_skin'

examples.title: Add and remove influences
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
a = cmds.joint(name="a")
cmds.select(clear=True)
b = cmds.joint(name="b", position=(0, 2, 0))
mesh = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
skin = cmds.skinCluster(a, mesh, toSelectedBones=True)[0]

cmds.skinCluster(skin, edit=True, addInfluence=b, weight=0)
print(cmds.skinCluster(skin, query=True, influence=True))  # ['a', 'b']

cmds.skinCluster(skin, edit=True, removeInfluence=b)
print(cmds.skinCluster(skin, query=True, influence=True))  # ['a']

examples.title: Influences that actually affect some points
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
a = cmds.joint(name="a")
cmds.select(clear=True)
b = cmds.joint(name="b", position=(0, 100, 0))
mesh = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
skin = cmds.skinCluster([a, b], mesh, toSelectedBones=True)[0]
cmds.skinPercent(skin, mesh + ".vtx[*]", transformValue=[(a, 1.0)])

print(cmds.skinCluster(skin, query=True, weightedInfluence=True))  # ['a']

examples.title: Unbind
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
jnt = cmds.joint(name="jnt")
mesh = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
skin = cmds.skinCluster(jnt, mesh, toSelectedBones=True)[0]

cmds.skinCluster(skin, edit=True, unbind=True)
print(cmds.ls(type="skinCluster"))  # []

gotchas: Influence names are returned as the shortest unique path. A joint named `top` comes back as `root|top` because a default camera is also called `top`.
Pass `toSelectedBones=True` when binding to specific joints; otherwise Maya can bind to the whole hierarchy below them.
Joints that are already bound can't be bound again to the same mesh; one mesh has one skinCluster unless `multi=True`.
`maximumInfluences` limits binding, but painting can exceed it unless `obeyMaxInfluences=True`.
The skinCluster is usually found through history: `cmds.ls(cmds.listHistory(mesh), type="skinCluster")`.

examples.title: Read the weights of one vertex
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
a = cmds.joint(name="a")
cmds.select(clear=True)
b = cmds.joint(name="b", position=(0, 1, 0))
mesh = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
skin = cmds.skinCluster([a, b], mesh, toSelectedBones=True)[0]

cmds.skinPercent(skin, mesh + ".vtx[0]", transformValue=[(a, 0.25), (b, 0.75)])
influences = cmds.skinPercent(skin, mesh + ".vtx[0]", query=True, transform=None)
weights = cmds.skinPercent(skin, mesh + ".vtx[0]", query=True, value=True)
print(dict(zip(influences, [round(w, 3) for w in weights])))  # {'a': 0.25, 'b': 0.75}

examples.title: Set weights on many vertices and prune small ones
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.select(clear=True)
a = cmds.joint(name="a")
cmds.select(clear=True)
b = cmds.joint(name="b", position=(0, 1, 0))
mesh = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
skin = cmds.skinCluster([a, b], mesh, toSelectedBones=True)[0]

cmds.skinPercent(skin, mesh + ".vtx[0:7]", transformValue=[(a, 0.99), (b, 0.01)])
cmds.skinPercent(skin, mesh + ".vtx[0:7]", pruneWeights=0.05)
print(cmds.skinPercent(skin, mesh + ".vtx[5]", query=True, value=True))  # [1.0, 0.0]

gotchas: Setting a weight renormalizes the others. Set all influences for a point in one `transformValue` list.
`query=True, transform=None` returns influence names in the same order as `value=True` weights.
`skinPercent` is slow on large meshes (one call per component). For bulk reads and writes, use `MFnSkinCluster.getWeights`/`setWeights` from the OpenMaya API.

examples.title: Group a script into one undo step
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.undoInfo(state=True, infinity=True)
cmds.undoInfo(openChunk=True, chunkName="make_boxes")
try:
    for i in range(3):
        cmds.polyCube(name="box%d" % i)
finally:
    cmds.undoInfo(closeChunk=True)

cmds.undo()
print(cmds.ls("box*", type="transform"))  # []

examples.title: A reusable decorator
Is undo on?
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cmds.undoInfo(state=True)
print(cmds.undoInfo(query=True, state=True))  # True

gotchas: Always close a chunk in a `finally` block. An unclosed chunk makes one huge undo step of everything that follows.
`state=False` clears the undo queue. Use `stateWithoutFlush=False` to pause undo without losing history, and turn it back on right after.
In `mayapy`, undo is off by default; turn it on with `undoInfo(state=True)` if a script relies on it.

examples.title: A tool window that replaces itself
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

WINDOW = "myToolWindow"

def show():
    if cmds.window(WINDOW, exists=True):
        cmds.deleteUI(WINDOW)
    cmds.window(WINDOW, title="My Tool", widthHeight=(300, 120), sizeable=True)
    cmds.columnLayout(adjustableColumn=True, rowSpacing=6)
    name_field = cmds.textFieldGrp(label="Name", text="box")
    cmds.button(label="Create", command=lambda *_: cmds.polyCube(name=cmds.textFieldGrp(name_field, query=True, text=True)))
    cmds.showWindow(WINDOW)

show()

examples.title: Remember size and position between sessions
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

if cmds.window("prefsWindow", exists=True):
    cmds.deleteUI("prefsWindow")
cmds.window("prefsWindow", title="Remembers its size", widthHeight=(400, 200))
cmds.columnLayout()
cmds.text(label="Resize me and reopen.")
cmds.showWindow("prefsWindow")
# Maya saves the size under windowPref; remove it to reset:
# cmds.windowPref("prefsWindow", remove=True)

gotchas: Creating a window with an existing name fails. Delete the old one first with `deleteUI`.
Maya remembers window size and position (`windowPref`), so `widthHeight` is ignored after the first time. Remove the pref or pass `resizeToFitChildren` to reset.
Commands on controls in Python receive an extra argument; use `lambda *_:` or accept `*args`.
For dockable tools use `workspaceControl` instead of `window`.

gotchas: `uiScript` runs again when Maya restores the workspace, from a fresh state. It must import your module and rebuild the UI, not rely on variables from the session that created it.

summary: Sets and queries transformations: translation, rotation, scale, pivots and matrices, in object or world space.
returns: With `query`, the requested values as a flat list, e.g. `[x, y, z]`. Otherwise nothing.

flags.objectSpace: Values are in the object's own space.
flags.reflection: Turn reflection on, so component moves are mirrored.
flags.centerPivotsOnComponents: Move the pivots to the center of the selected components.
flags.reflectionAboutBBox: Reflect across the center of the bounding box.
flags.boundingBoxInvisible: Query only: like `boundingBox`, but also includes invisible children.
flags.preserveUV: When moving components, adjust UVs so textures stay in place.
flags.worldSpaceDistance: Treat translation values as world space distances, even when setting them in object space.
flags.boundingBox: Query only: the bounding box as xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax. World space unless `objectSpace` is used.
flags.rotateAxis: The rotate axis orientation, in degrees.
flags.pivots: Set the rotate and scale pivots together. Query returns both.
flags.relative: Add the values to the current ones instead of replacing them.
flags.preserve: When changing pivots or `rotateAxis`, keep the object in place.
flags.rotateTranslation: Translation that compensates for the rotate pivot, so the object stays in place.
flags.absolute: Set values as absolute. This is the default.
flags.matrix: The transformation matrix as 16 values. Query returns the local matrix, or world matrix with `worldSpace`.
flags.translation: Translation. With `worldSpace` it's the world position of the object's origin, not of its pivot.
flags.reflectionTolerance: Distance tolerance for finding the mirrored component.
flags.scaleTranslation: Translation that compensates for the scale pivot, so the object stays in place.
flags.zeroTransformPivots: Reset the pivots to the origin without moving the object.
flags.parentSpace: Values are in the parent's space.
flags.euler: With `relative` rotation, keep the resulting rotation values close to the current ones instead of wrapping.
flags.centerPivots: Move the rotate and scale pivots to the center of the bounding box.
flags.deletePriorHistory: For components, delete construction history before moving them.

examples.title: World position of an object
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

grp = cmds.group(empty=True, name="grp")
cmds.move(0, 10, 0, grp)
loc = cmds.spaceLocator(name="loc")[0]
loc = cmds.parent(loc, grp)[0]
cmds.setAttr(loc + ".translate", 3, 0, 0)   # local offset from the parent

print(cmds.xform(loc, query=True, translation=True))  # [3.0, 0.0, 0.0]
print(cmds.xform(loc, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True))  # [3.0, 10.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Snap one object to another (position and rotation)
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

target = cmds.spaceLocator(name="target")[0]
cmds.xform(target, worldSpace=True, translation=(1, 2, 3), rotation=(0, 90, 0))
obj = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

cmds.xform(obj, worldSpace=True, matrix=cmds.xform(target, query=True, worldSpace=True, matrix=True))
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(obj, query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)])  # [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
print([round(v, 3) for v in cmds.xform(obj, query=True, worldSpace=True, rotation=True)])  # [0.0, 90.0, 0.0]

examples.title: Move pivots without moving the object
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box", height=2)[0]
cmds.xform(cube, worldSpace=True, pivots=(0, -1, 0))

print(cmds.xform(cube, query=True, worldSpace=True, rotatePivot=True))  # [0.0, -1.0, 0.0]
print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".translate"))  # [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]

examples.title: Bounding box
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box", width=2, height=4, depth=6)[0]
cmds.move(10, 0, 0, cube)

print(cmds.xform(cube, query=True, boundingBox=True, worldSpace=True))  # [9.0, -2.0, -3.0, 11.0, 2.0, 3.0]

examples.title: Relative moves and vertex positions
examples.code:
from maya import cmds

cube = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]
cmds.xform(cube, relative=True, translation=(0, 1, 0))
cmds.xform(cube, relative=True, translation=(0, 1, 0))
print(cmds.getAttr(cube + ".translateY"))  # 2.0

cmds.xform(cube + ".vtx[0]", worldSpace=True, translation=(-1, 0, 1))
print(cmds.xform(cube + ".vtx[0]", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True))  # [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0]

gotchas: Without `worldSpace=True`, queries return local values. That's the most common bug when snapping objects.
A world space `translation` query returns the position of the object's origin, not its pivot. Use `rotatePivot` for the pivot.
Querying several components returns one flat list: `[x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1, …]`. Chunk it by 3.
Rotations set in world space are converted into the object's rotate order, so values can look different from what you passed while producing the same orientation.

xformConstraint.name: xformConstraint
summary: Sets or queries the transform constraint used by the Move tool: none, surface or edge.

flags.live: Query only: whether the constraint uses a live surface.
